transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivera (Redwood SE), Clara Zhou (Redwood CSM); Priya Menon (CISO, Orchid), Daniel Wu (Head of Platform), Sara Lee (Compliance), Tom Alvarez (Infra)

Summary (auto):
Short sync to walk through Redwood assurance portal access, SCOPe of SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, mapping controls to Orchid internal control matrix, and clarify encryption/KMS and data residency constraints. Agree next steps around document share and SE deep-dive scheduling.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya (Orchid CISO): hi, Priya here. thanks.
[00:08] Daniel: Daniel, morning.
[00:10] Sara: Sara, good to meet.
[00:12] Tom: Tom here.
[00:15] Maya: and Ethan and Clara with me, Ethan will cover KMS and infra bits. this is a posture/readout sync, not legal signoff. sound right?

[02:10] Ethan (Redwood SE): cool, i'll jump into the technical gaps we typically see. quick context: Redwood exposes an assurance portal where customers can access audit artifacts, SOC reports, configuration screenshots, and a control mapping. For customers needing stricter residency we support region-restricted storage and private deployments.

[04:00] Priya: can you clarify what you mean by "assurance portal" — it's a separate console from the Redwood Console? we need to know who gets access and how it's logged.
[04:15] Maya: good q. it's the assurance portal (we sometimes call it the trust portal) — separate access with RBAC. you get granular invites (read-only or admin) and every object access is logged into audit logs with retention settings. access is SSO via SAML/SCIM sync with your IdP. there is a link we will send.

[06:30] Sara: retention — we plan to retain evidence for 3 years for ISO. what are your typical retention windows for artifacts and logs? and is log export available?
[06:45] Ethan: artifacts: up to 7 years archived, default 13 months hot; audit logs: 13 months by default, can extend to multiyear via the add-on. logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3 in an encrypted form. some customers push to a customer-owned S3 in dedicated mode.

[09:10] Daniel: about the SOC 2 doc itself — do you provide redacted Type II? and does the portal include the control narrative mapping so we can map to our internal matrix?
[09:25] Maya: yes, we'll upload the redacted SOC 2 Type II and an ISO 27001 summary. we also provide a CSV/worksheet mapping Redwood controls to the SOC/ISO clauses so your compliance team can crosswalk.

[11:40] Priya: KMS — we are strict: we use an HSM-backed KMS on-prem. we need to know if Redwood can support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key, external KMS) for private deployments or at least envelope encryption with key control.
[12:00] Ethan: we support BYOK in Dedicated and Private modes; for hosted we offer envelope encryption where keys can be in a customer KMS with an optional HSM flow. for Private (VPC/on-prem) you can run our control plane and connect to your HSM — there are a few config examples I'll share.

[14:20] Tom: any constraints around model caching / KV cache and residency? does cached data ever leave the region?
[14:35] Ethan: caching is region-aware; by default we keep KV cache local to the serving region. for strict residency customers we pin inference workloads to region and ensure caches are on region-resident storage. there are edge cases with cross-region failover where we use pre-authorized fallbacks; if you want zero-cross-region traffic that's possible in Private deployment.

[17:00] Sara: authentication/SSO — we use Okta. can you support SCIM for user provisioning and SAML for SSO with per-role RBAC? we need RBAC that maps to control owners.
[17:20] Maya: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC roles: org admin, security reader, billing, dev, se. We can create custom roles and map SCIM attributes. All role assignments are logged in the audit trail.

[19:40] Priya: audit logs — we need immutable logs for certain controls. can we get append-only export with checksums?
[19:55] Ethan: our audit export supports integrity checks — we sign batches and provide a rolling checksum; for Private we can configure write-once buckets and supply retention policies that meet ISO/SOC requirements.

[22:30] Daniel: question about evidence collection cadence — for SOC 2 we expect quarterly evidence for some controls, annual for others. how do you handle ad-hoc evidence requests from auditors?
[22:45] Clara (Redwood CSM): we typically provide a pull request to the assurance portal with an evidence bundle. customers can invite their auditors directly with time-limited access or we can create an export package and deliver. turnaround times vary but we aim for 3-5 business days for most artifacts.

[25:10] Priya: we have a nuance — our product team also wants to run PII-parsing evals that will send telemetry logs for prompt improvement. is that considered customer data and how is it segregated?
[25:28] Maya: good to flag. telemetry for product/evals is treated as customer data; in Hosted we segregate per-tenant and can opt-out of aggregate telemetry. For guaranteed isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll include guidance on turning off telemetry and recommended config.

[28:40] Tom: encryption-in-transit specifics? TLS versions? mutual TLS for service-to-service?
[28:55] Ethan: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported; for Private we support mTLS for internal service connections; front-door is TLS with certs managed by Redwood or customer-managed certs on Private.

[31:15] Sara: is there a documented control mapping for ISO 27001 Annex A to your platform features? auditors like to see control traceability.
[31:30] Maya: yes we have an Annex A crosswalk that maps our features and procedures to ISO clauses and sample evidence. we'll attach that.

[33:40] Daniel: what about data residency — we are EU-only for regulated data. can you guarantee all PII stays in eu-west-1?
[33:55] Ethan: yes, with Private or Dedicated in region we can enforce region-only data plane and storage. for Hosted we have region tenancy options; you'll have to contract region restrictions — we can include in the SLA.

[36:00] Priya: incident response — do you provide SLA on notification times? we need breach notification within X hours and post-incident reports.
[36:15] Clara: our standard enterprise SLA includes 72-hour notification for incidents impacting confidentiality; higher tiers and dedicated contracts can get 24-hour or faster. IR postmortems and timeline are provided as part of incident reporting.

[38:50] Maya: circling back to control owners — Sara, if you provide a list of controls you want mapped and the cadence we can create a custom evidence playbook. also we'll add Daniel/Tom to the SE deep-dive for KMS specifics.

[41:05] Tom: for KMS we'll need example key policies and ephemeral key rotation examples. also, key recovery process if we rotate outside of Redwood.
[41:20] Ethan: got it. i will prepare sample policies (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and a generic HSM flow). we'll show envelope encryption examples and an option where customer retains root key in HSM.

[44:00] Priya: one objection — we've seen a competitor promise full BYOK for hosted with zero key exposure. is that realistic?
[44:15] Maya: caution there — for true zero-exposure in a multi-tenant hosted service is extremely hard. most implementations use envelope encryption where master key material is customer-controlled but some metadata may still be held. Dedicated/Private gives true physical separation and better guarantees. we prefer being transparent about tradeoffs.

[47:10] Daniel: pricing — can you share delta between Hosted with extended retention add-on vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private?
[47:25] Maya: yes, we'll include a pricing sketch in follow-up (not formal quote). Hosted + retention add-on typically has lower upfront but higher unit cost; Dedicated has commit pricing and better unit economics; Private includes platform licensing. We'll send a short spreadsheet.

[50:00] Clara: ok to recap next steps?
[50:05] Maya: i will: 1) share redacted SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary, Annex A crosswalk, and portal invite by 9/19; 2) ethan will prepare KMS/HSM config samples and key policy examples by 9/24; 3) orchid to confirm EU-only residency and list of KMS providers by 9/19; 4) schedule SE deep dive week of 9/22. anything else?

[52:30] Sara: please also include evidence cadence template and auditor access instructions.
[52:40] Maya: will do.
[53:00] Priya: thanks all, this was helpful.
[53:10] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and add items to the CRM.

End of transcript.
